constraints.text: Request: a fresh token, once a minute, only for an inbox reply
Acknowledge: the right token returns the reply subject and is spent
RejectAck: a wrong or repeated token changes nothing
emitted t <= 1: one channel event per request however often it is delivered
constraints.verifiedBy: the first requests once and runs the emitter twice: one frame, kind channel_check, and the token it names is acknowledged once; the second requests again 59 s later: still one frame; the daemon test asks twice and the client sees one event. They exercise the count of events per request; none delivers the same request frame to the client twice and checks the client's emitter sends once (the emitter is fed by ChannelCheck.request, not by a daemon frame). Medium

constraints.text: relayed t <= 1: the acknowledgement is relayed to the doctor once however often it arrives
constraints.verifiedBy: a real daemon over a push relay: the first ack publishes one CheckAck to the reply subject; a second ack answers 'not accepted' and the published count stays 1; a wrong token publishes nothing

the emitter test sends nothing before initialised and exactly one channel_check frame after; PR 685's test publishes a request on the real bus and the client's sink receives one channel_check carrying the daemon's 128-bit token, which channel_ack then relays once. 'sent => emitted = 1' is exercised as 'one frame per accepted request'; the property is close to a tautology of the code. The second half is not on main until PR 685 merges

constraints.text: DeliverRequest: at-least-once delivery of the request frame to the session client
constraints.verifiedBy: a pending check is delivered to the first subscription, then a second subscription of the same session receives unread and the same request again, before any acknowledgement; the ack is then relayed once

constraints.text: SendEvent: needs the request to have reached the client
constraints.verifiedBy: PR 685: no channel_check frame exists in the client's sink until the request frame has crossed the daemon, and the event carries the daemon's token: the client sends only for a request that reached it. The daemon test shows the pending request is delivered after the unread summary. The emitter's 'waits for the client to be initialised' test does NOT exercise this constraint (it gates on initialize, not on request delivery). Covered only once PR 685 merges

constraints.text: DeliverRequest: a request frame replayed after the acknowledgement (afterAck >= 1) makes no second event and no second relayed ack
constraints.verifiedBy: after an acknowledged token, a new subscription gets unread and no further request event within 0.3 s, and a second channel_ack relays nothing (still one CheckAck). The daemon side of the constraint; the client's emitter is not given the replay
